source.note: Figures describe the Espace Killy (Tignes–Val d'Isère), the area covered by the standard day pass. Search summary of Tignes lift pages and Wikipedia: Espace Killy (Tignes–Val d'Isère, one ticket): 300 km of marked pistes; 90 lifts = 2 funiculars, 4 cable cars, 4 gondolas, 44 chairlifts, 36 surface lifts; one result states that '87 ski lifts' uplift 64,480 skiers and snowboarders per hour (likely an older lift count). Runs: 156 = 23 green (15%), 66 blue (42%), 40 red (26%), 27 black (17%). Perce-Neige funicular (Val Claret to the Grande Motte): 3,491 m long, 3,600 passengers/hour. Tignes-only totals not found.

Piste reference data — confirm at source. Only features Piste is confident about are set; everything else is unknown (null), not 'not offered'. Ski schools (e.g. ESF) and rental shops operate in the resort villages

character: Tignes is a group of high villages (Val Claret, Le Lac, Le Lavachet, Tignes 1800, Les Boisses and Les Brévières) that shares the Espace Killy with Val d'Isère: about 300 km of pistes and around 90 lifts. The Grande Motte glacier, reached by the Perce-Neige underground funicular, gives one of the longest winter seasons in the Alps, from late November into May.
learning: The Espace Killy has 23 green and 66 blue runs by one count (search summary). Reference: the main villages have beginner areas; the altitude (2,100 m at Le Lac) means cold, exposed conditions early and late in the season. Confirm beginner-lift access and lessons locally.
